title: Desk Guidance: Patient Payment Plan Schedule Length After an Assistance Pause
content:
The schedule of a **Patient Payment Plan** after an assistance pause is figured as follows.

**Open application and receipt date.** A financial assistance application of the patient is open when one of the patient's financial assistance cases in the Financial Assistance Program (Charity Care) stands in submitted or pending documents status, a submitted case being taken first. Its receipt date is that case's application date. With no open application nothing is paused.

**Whole months.** Whole months between two dates are counted the calendar way: a month is complete only once the later date's day number reaches the earlier date's day number (from the 31st, a month without that day is not yet complete at its last day), and a later date before the starting date gives a negative count.

**Which installments are considered.** Due dates fall on the plan's due day each month from the first due date, so the installments falling due on or before a date are the whole months from the first due date to that date plus one; the installments a pause considers are those falling due after the receipt date and on or after the plan's next due date (every one after the receipt date when the plan has no next due date), a receipt date before the first due date counting as one month before it so that no installment is counted before the first due date, up to the end of the pause window. Put as a count: the considered installments in the window are the installments falling due on or before the end of the window, less the larger of the installments falling due on or before the receipt date (never fewer than none) and the installments falling due before the next due date (only the former when the plan has no next due date), and never fewer than none.

**Pause window.** The pause window ends on the handling date.

**Pause allowance.** No more installments are paused than the pause allowance, one installment for each full 30 days of the pause period; the pause period is the tier's assistance pause days. A remainder of fewer than 30 days adds nothing.

**Schedule length.** The schedule length after the pause is the plan's current number of scheduled installments plus the paused installments, never longer than the longest paused schedule, which is the tier's maximum term, and never shorter than the current number of scheduled installments.

**Order.** The pause period and the pause window are settled first, the paused installments are then held to the pause allowance and added to the current number of scheduled installments, the longest paused schedule is applied to that sum next, and the rule that the schedule is never left shorter than the current one is applied last.

### Worked example (hypothetical figures)

A plan due on the 15th, first due date 15 January, next due date 15 April, 30 installments scheduled, on a tier with 60 assistance pause days and a 36-installment maximum term. The open application was received on 20 March; the handling date is 25 June.
- Installments falling due on or before 25 June: 5 whole months plus one, 6. On or before 20 March: 2 plus one, 3. Before 15 April: 3. The larger is 3, so 3 installments are considered in the window (April, May, June).
- Pause allowance: 60 days hold 2 full periods of 30 days, so 2.
- Paused: 3 held to 2. Schedule: 30 plus 2 is 32, within 36 and not below 30, so 32 scheduled installments.
